 Mariners Rumors: Teams are trying to change Seattle's mind on Logan Gilbert trade 
 Good luck with that. By Zachary Rymer | Nov 17, 2026, 11:00 PM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Logan Gilbert isn't meant to be one of the expendable members of the Seattle Mariners' six-deep starting rotation, but there's nothing stopping teams from asking. And they are.
--> Logan Gilbert isn't meant to be one of the expendable members of the Seattle Mariners' six-deep starting rotation, but there's nothing stopping teams from asking. And they are.
 According to Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon of The Athletic , Gilbert is one of several prominent pitchers who are drawing trade attention despite the fact that they are due for free agency after 2027. They say other clubs are merely "inquiring," which should not necessarily be taken for an indication that the Mariners are listening.
--> According to Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon of The Athletic , Gilbert is one of several prominent pitchers who are drawing trade attention despite the fact that they are due for free agency after 2027. They say other clubs are merely "inquiring," which should not necessarily be taken for an indication that the Mariners are listening.
 At least for now, the circumstances surrounding Gilbert and other starters in the post-2027 boat (i.e., MacKenzie Gore and Nick Lodolo) are awkward because of the impending lockout. Nobody knows how much of next season will be played, which makes it difficult to assess just how valuable those who are only controlled through next year are really worth.

Nobody knows how much of next season will be played, which makes it difficult to assess just how valuable those who are only controlled through next year are really worth.
 There's been speculation that swapping prospective post-2027 free agents one-for-one could be a viable strategy. Yet there are only so many hypothetical trades that fit the bill, and obviously not all of them are workable on both ends. To wit, a potential deal in which the Mariners send Gilbert to the Cleveland Guardians for Steven Kwan is a hard sell .

 Besides which, FanSided's own Robert Murray had some intel on Gilbert that snuck out during his Reddit AMA from last week: "I also did not get the sense Logan Gilbert is someone they want to move. I expect him to stay."
--> Besides which, FanSided's own Robert Murray had some intel on Gilbert that snuck out during his Reddit AMA from last week: "I also did not get the sense Logan Gilbert is someone they want to move. I expect him to stay."
 Even if it's been a minute since he was the next man up after Cal Raleigh, there may yet be hope in the organization that Gilbert could be signed to an extension. Either that, or they just prefer to keep him atop the rotation next year even if it could be his last as a Mariner.
--> Even if it's been a minute since he was the next man up after Cal Raleigh, there may yet be hope in the organization that Gilbert could be signed to an extension. Either that, or they just prefer to keep him atop the rotation next year even if it could be his last as a Mariner.
 According to Alden Gonzalez of ESPN, it's Bryce Miller, Emerson Hancock and George Kirby who are the "more attainable" members of Seattle's rotation surplus. They only have so much trade value between them , but that's only a problem if you're only vision of a trade involves bringing back a superstar such as Elly De La Cruz. That would be nice, but so would someone like, say, Jordan Westburg or Matt Shaw.

They only have so much trade value between them , but that's only a problem if you're only vision of a trade involves bringing back a superstar such as Elly De La Cruz. That would be nice, but so would someone like, say, Jordan Westburg or Matt Shaw.
 If teams are calling the Mariners about Gilbert, there's no reason for Jerry Dipoto and Justin Hollander not to listen. But unless they can somehow cash him in for a controllable bat or two, it's hard to imagine a swap involving another prospective post-2027 free agent that makes sense. Maybe William Contreras, Trevor Megill or Jeremy Peña, but those are all for the "Not Bloody Likely" folder.
